transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I came in because I just feel like I can’t settle inside myself anymore. It’s hard to explain without sounding dramatic, but it’s like I’m in my own skin and it doesn’t feel quiet in there. Even when I’m tired — and I mean really worn out, where I know I should just sit down and rest — there’s this feeling like I have to get up, do the next thing, move on to something else, check something, start something.

It’s not just being “busy,” you know? It feels more like an inner push, like I’m being prodded from the inside. I’ll tell myself, “Just sit still for a minute,” and then almost right away I feel like I need to jump up again. It’s gotten to where I feel uncomfortable just being still, and that’s really what made me think I need to talk to someone, because I’m exhausted but I still can’t seem to settle.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I wouldn’t say I’ve had, like, a clear stretch where I suddenly felt wonderful and full of energy and didn’t need sleep. That doesn’t sound quite like me.

My thoughts do feel busy sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean by “racing.” It’s more that I have a lot going on in my head and I have trouble slowing it down, but I can’t really point to a period where it was unusual in that way, with needing less sleep or feeling powered up. If anything, I’m often tired, even when I still can’t seem to settle.
Can you describe what happens when you try to relax or when you’re in a situation where you’re supposed to be still — do you feel restless, tense, or like something bad is going to happen?

Yes… restless is probably the best word, though it almost doesn’t feel strong enough. It’s not so much that I think something bad is going to happen, exactly. It’s more like I just cannot get comfortable being still. Like I’m sitting there and my body is technically in the chair, but inside I’m already halfway up, if that makes sense.

If I try to relax, I’ll tell myself, “Just sit here, just rest for a bit, you’re tired,” because I really am worn out a lot of the time. But then almost immediately I get this urge to jump up and do the next thing — check something, straighten something, start some little task, anything. It feels like being in my own skin is uncomfortable when I’m not moving.

And it’s frustrating because I know I should be able to sit still. I’m not trying to be busy for the sake of being busy. It feels more like there’s this pressure inside me pushing me along, even when I don’t have the energy for it. So yes, when I’m supposed to be still, I feel very restless — not peaceful, not settled. I feel like I have to get up.
Do you ever feel a lot of worry or fear that seems out of proportion to what's actually happening around you?

I don’t think fear is really the word I’d use. I mean, I worry about things like anybody does, and sometimes I can get worked up in my head trying to sort things out, but I don’t usually feel like I’m scared of something that isn’t really there, if that’s what you mean.

It’s more… I don’t know, I’m trying to be accurate. I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there thinking something terrible is about to happen. It’s not like that kind of fear. If I seem wound up, it’s not usually because I believe there’s some big danger around me. It’s more that I feel unsettled, and then I might start fussing over little things because I can’t quite leave them alone.

So, no, I haven’t really noticed a lot of out-of-proportion fear. Worry, maybe sometimes, but not in a way where I’d say it’s the main thing or that it feels bigger than what’s happening.
Have you had periods where you felt down, sad, or lost interest in things that usually matter to you?

I’m not really sure. I mean… I have days where I feel worn out or discouraged, especially when I can’t get myself together the way I think I should. But I don’t know if I’d call it being “down” in the way you mean.

I still care about things, at least I think I do. It’s more that sometimes I don’t follow through or I put things off, and then from the outside maybe it could look like I’ve lost interest. But inside it doesn’t feel like I stopped caring. It’s more like I get stuck, or I can’t quite make myself start.

So… I don’t think I’ve had a clear period where everything felt sad and empty, or where things that matter to me suddenly didn’t matter. Not that I can point to, anyway.
Do you find yourself moving around a lot, like pacing, fidgeting, or tapping your hands or feet, even when you're trying to stay still?

Yes, absolutely. I’m doing it more than I realize half the time. Like even in church meetings, where you’re supposed to be quiet and respectful and still, I’ll catch myself tapping my foot, or rubbing the edge of my purse over and over with my fingers, or shifting around in the chair.

And I try to stop because I don’t want to be distracting, especially sitting with the other ladies there, but then a few minutes later I’m doing something else with my hands or feet. Sometimes I notice because the ladies beside me start looking over, and then I feel embarrassed, like, “Oh, I’m doing it again.” It’s not that I’m trying to be rude or impatient. I just feel like my body keeps needing to move, even when I’m trying very hard to sit still.
Have you noticed this inner restlessness or need to move getting worse when you start or change any medications?

I’m not sure I can tie it neatly to starting or changing a medicine, no. I wish I could give you a clean answer like, “Yes, it happened right after this,” but that’s not really how I’ve been thinking of it.

What I can say is that the reason I came in is because lately I feel like I just cannot settle inside my own skin. That’s the best way I know how to put it. It’s like there’s this push in me to get up and do the next thing, or fix the next thing, or move around, even when I’m worn out and I know I should just sit still. My body will be tired, but inside I’m still sort of… revved up, I guess.

So I don’t know if medication changes have made it worse or not. I haven’t noticed that pattern clearly. It’s more that the restlessness itself has gotten hard to ignore.
Have you ever felt like you had to move because of an uncomfortable feeling inside your body, even if you couldn’t quite explain what was bothering you?

Yes… yes, that’s actually a good way to say it. It’s hard for me to explain because it’s not always like pain or something I can point to, like, “My leg hurts” or “my back hurts.” It’s more like this uncomfortable feeling inside me, like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore.

I’ll be sitting there, and I know I’m tired, I know I should just sit still for a minute, but there’s this feeling like I have to jump up and do the next thing. Like I need to move, or start something, or check on something, even if there isn’t really a good reason right then. It’s almost like my body and my mind don’t agree with each other. My body is worn out, but inside I feel pushed, like I can’t just be still.

And it bothers me because I’ll think, “Why can’t I just sit here like a normal person?” I don’t even always know what I’m trying to fix or what I’m supposed to be doing. I just feel like I have to get up and do something. So yes, I think that’s been a big part of why I came in.
Is this inner restlessness something you feel most of the time, even when you're not in situations that might make you anxious or require you to sit still, like when you're alone at home relaxing?

Yes, I do. It’s not only when I’m somewhere I’m supposed to sit still, like a meeting or church or something formal. It happens even when I’m home and there’s no one there to bother me and nothing I have to prove to anybody.

That’s actually part of what worries me, because I’ll be alone at home and I’ll think, “Okay, I can finally sit down and relax,” and then I just… can’t. I might be worn out, really tired, and still I feel like I need to get up and do the next thing. Not always because there’s some urgent thing that has to be done, but because I feel unsettled inside, like I can’t settle inside my own skin.

It’s like my body should be resting, but something in me is saying, “Get up, move, do something.” And I’ll sit for a minute and then I’m up again, or I’m thinking about what I should jump to next. So yes, it’s most of the time lately, not just in situations that make me nervous or where I’m being expected to sit still. That’s really why I came in, because it’s gotten to where I don’t feel like I can just be still anymore.
Have you ever felt this inner restlessness or need to move after taking any medications, especially ones like antidepressants or antipsychotics?

I honestly don’t know that I can say it happened after taking a certain medication. I don’t want to give you the wrong idea or act like I’ve clearly noticed, “Oh, I took this pill and then I couldn’t sit still,” because I haven’t really tracked it that way.

What I can say is that the reason I came in is this feeling that I just cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. It’s like I have to jump up and do the next thing, even when I’m worn out and should be sitting still. I’ll be tired, and I’ll know there’s no reason I need to get up right that second, but inside it feels like something is pushing me to move or do something.

So, as far as antidepressants or those kinds of medicines, I can’t honestly connect it to that. The restlessness is definitely there, though, and it’s gotten hard for me to ignore.
Has this inner restlessness made it hard for you to function in your usual daily activities, or caused you a lot of distress?

Yes, it really has. I wish I could say it was just annoying, like just this private uncomfortable feeling, but it’s gone past that.

My family has had to step in with things I used to handle myself, like bills and paperwork, because I either don’t sit down long enough to finish them or I jump from one thing to another and leave it half done. And then it piles up, and then I feel ashamed, and then someone has to help me sort through it. That’s been hard, because I’ve always wanted to be seen as someone who can manage her own affairs.

And it’s affected other people too, not just at home. At church, and with the garden group, there have been times when I said I would take care of something or be responsible for part of a plan, and then I dropped it or didn’t follow through the way I should have. People had to redo plans or cover for me, and I could tell it frustrated them, even if they were kind about it.

That part really bothers me. I feel embarrassed, honestly. These are groups I care about, and I don’t want to be unreliable. But lately I feel like people don’t quite trust that they can count on me the way they used to, and that makes me feel awful. So yes, it’s caused a lot of distress, and it’s definitely interfering with my normal life.
Have you ever experienced this kind of restlessness or need to move when you started, stopped, or changed the dose of a medication, even if it was a long time ago?

I’m not sure, honestly. I’ve been trying to think back, because I know you’re asking whether there was some clear point where I started or stopped a medicine, or the dose changed, and then this restlessness showed up.

But I can’t really say that. I don’t have a memory of, “Oh, that happened right after a medication change.” I just don’t want to guess and accidentally make it sound like there’s a connection when I haven’t actually noticed one.

I mean, it may be that there were medication changes over the years and I just didn’t pay attention closely enough, but as I’m sitting here trying to remember, nothing stands out to me like that. What stands out is the restlessness itself and how hard it’s been to settle down, but I can’t tie it to starting, stopping, or changing a dose of something.

Do you ever feel driven to do certain things over and over, like checking, counting, or fixing, because you can't get certain thoughts out of your head or because you feel something bad will happen if you don't?

I don’t think so, not in the way you’re describing. I mean, I do sometimes go back and recheck things, but I think that’s more because I get distracted or I don’t trust that I finished something properly, not because I have a specific thought like, “If I don’t check this three times, something terrible will happen.”

I don’t really count things or have rituals like that, at least not that I’ve noticed. And I don’t feel like I’m fixing things over and over to stop some bad event from happening. It’s more that I’ll lose track, or I’ll feel unsettled and then I’m not sure what I already did. But I can’t say I have those stuck thoughts you’re talking about, where they force me to do a certain action in a certain way.
Have you always had trouble sitting still or feeling calm, even going back to when you were younger, or is this something that started more recently in your life?

Oh, it goes way back. It’s not something that just started recently, even though it feels worse or more noticeable now.

I actually remember seeing comments from teachers when I was in grade school — or my mother would mention them — that I was “bright but careless,” that kind of thing. They’d say I lost papers, talked when I wasn’t supposed to, didn’t stay with my work, or needed reminders to stay in my seat and finish what I was doing. At the time, I think people just thought I was careless or not trying hard enough, because I could understand the schoolwork, but I was always being corrected for the way I went about it.

So yes, the sitting still and settling myself, that has been there since I was young. It’s just that when you’re a child, people scold you or redirect you, and you don’t necessarily think of it as a pattern until much later.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more where you felt extremely upbeat, unusually confident, or so energetic that you hardly needed sleep?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt keyed up or couldn’t settle, but not in the way you’re saying — like several days where I was unusually upbeat or full of confidence and barely sleeping and still feeling great.

I’m trying to be careful, because my energy can feel all over the place, and sometimes I’ll stay up too late or get wound up, but I don’t remember a stretch where I thought, “Wow, I don’t need sleep,” or where I was on top of the world for days. If anything, when I don’t sleep enough, I usually feel worse, not better.

So as far as I can tell, no, I haven’t had that kind of period.
Have you ever had a time when your mood was elevated, you felt unusually good or irritable for several days, and you were doing things more quickly, taking more chances, or talking more than usual?

No, I don’t think I’ve had a time like that. I mean, I can get irritable, and I can talk more when I’m wound up or nervous or trying to explain myself, but I don’t remember it coming in a several-day stretch where my mood was unusually high or I felt like a different person.

And I don’t think I’ve had those times where I was suddenly doing everything faster, taking risks, or feeling unusually good in a way that other people would notice as odd. If I’m moving quickly or talking a lot, it’s usually more scattered than anything, not like I’m confident and energized for days. I’m trying to think back, but nothing like that really stands out to me.
Have you ever felt a strong urge to move your legs or a discomfort in your legs that only gets better when you move them, especially at night or when resting?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think I’ve noticed that as a clear pattern — like a strong urge in my legs that only gets better if I move them. I do shift around a lot when I’m sitting or trying to relax, but I can’t say it’s because of a specific uncomfortable feeling in my legs, especially at night.

So… I guess my answer would be no, not that I’m aware of. If it has happened, I haven’t recognized it that way.

Looking back at your adult life, have you often had trouble staying focused on tasks, felt constantly on the go, or struggled to organize your thoughts and activities, even when you weren’t under unusual stress?

Yes, the focus part especially. That’s been there a long time, not just when something stressful is going on.

Like, I can sit down with the senior center newsletter, or even something simple like a choir schedule, and I start out thinking, “Okay, I’m going to read this and make sure I know what’s happening.” And then a few minutes later I realize my eyes have been going over the same lines again and again, and I honestly couldn’t tell you what I just read. It’s not that the words are too hard or that I don’t care — it’s like my mind just slips away while I’m still looking at the page.

And then I’ll go back to the top and try again, and sometimes I do that two or three times. It makes me feel foolish, because these are not complicated things. They’re everyday things I should be able to keep track of. So yes, trouble staying focused has definitely been an issue for me as an adult.

Have you ever had a period of time lasting two weeks or more where you felt so down, hopeless, or uninterested in life that it was hard to function, or a time when you felt unusually high, overly confident, or so energetic that others noticed something was off?

I’m not sure I can say yes to either of those in a clear way. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt low or discouraged, like anyone does, especially when things pile up or I’m frustrated with myself, but I don’t know that I’ve had a solid two weeks where I was so hopeless or uninterested in life that I just couldn’t function. At least nothing that stands out to me that way.

And the unusually high part, no, I don’t think so. I’ve never had a stretch where I felt overly confident or so full of energy that other people were saying something was wrong. If anything, when I’m wound up, it’s more like I’m scattered or restless, not like I’m on top of the world.

So I guess my answer is… not that I’m aware of. I’d probably remember if it was that extreme, but I don’t think I’ve had that kind of episode.
Have you ever had a time when your mood was so low or so high that someone close to you expressed concern about the change, even if it didn’t last very long?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, people close to me have probably noticed when I’m irritated or overwhelmed or quieter than usual, but I can’t remember anyone saying they were worried because my mood seemed extremely low or unusually high.

I’m trying to think back, because sometimes family will say things like, “Are you okay?” or “You seem off today,” but that’s more in the normal kind of way, not like they were alarmed by a big change in me. I don’t recall anyone pulling me aside or saying, “You’re not acting like yourself,” because I was too down or too energized or anything like that.

So… no, not that I can remember. If it happened, it wasn’t something that stood out to me as a major mood change.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I can tie it neatly to starting or changing a medicine, no. I wish I could give you a clean answer like, “Yes, it happened right after this,” but that’s not really how I’ve been thinking of it.

What I can say is that the reason I came in is because lately I feel like I just cannot settle inside my own skin. That’s the best way I know how to put it. It’s like there’s this push in me to get up and do the next thing, or fix the next thing, or move around, even when I’m worn out and I know I should just sit still. My body will be tired, but inside I’m still sort of… revved up, I guess.

So I don’t know if medication changes have made it worse or not. I haven’t noticed that pattern clearly. It’s more that the restlessness itself has gotten hard to ignore.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences akathisia, which could suggest a medication-related side effect or a primary condition like F06.4 (psychological symptoms due to central nervous system stimulant intoxication or side effects of a drug).
doctor.question: Have you ever felt like you had to move because of an uncomfortable feeling inside your body, even if you couldn’t quite explain what was bothering you?

target_item.name: Feeling_Restless
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I feel like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore, like I have to jump up and do the next thing even when I am worn out and should be sitting still.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about an inner uncomfortable restlessness or need to move, which most directly matches feeling restless in adults.

patient.answer:
Yes… yes, that’s actually a good way to say it. It’s hard for me to explain because it’s not always like pain or something I can point to, like, “My leg hurts” or “my back hurts.” It’s more like this uncomfortable feeling inside me, like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore.

I’ll be sitting there, and I know I’m tired, I know I should just sit still for a minute, but there’s this feeling like I have to jump up and do the next thing. Like I need to move, or start something, or check on something, even if there isn’t really a good reason right then. It’s almost like my body and my mind don’t agree with each other. My body is worn out, but inside I feel pushed, like I can’t just be still.

And it bothers me because I’ll think, “Why can’t I just sit here like a normal person?” I don’t even always know what I’m trying to fix or what I’m supposed to be doing. I just feel like I have to get up and do something. So yes, I think that’s been a big part of why I came in.

doctor.intent: Determine if the restlessness is present at baseline or only in specific contexts, to differentiate between akathisia and other restlessness-related disorders.
doctor.question: Is this inner restlessness something you feel most of the time, even when you're not in situations that might make you anxious or require you to sit still, like when you're alone at home relaxing?

target_item.name: Feeling_Restless
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I feel like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore, like I have to jump up and do the next thing even when I am worn out and should be sitting still.
target_item.reason: The question directly asks about pervasive inner restlessness and a need to move even outside anxiety-provoking or sit-still situations, which matches the adult presentation of feeling restless.

patient.answer:
Yes, I do. It’s not only when I’m somewhere I’m supposed to sit still, like a meeting or church or something formal. It happens even when I’m home and there’s no one there to bother me and nothing I have to prove to anybody.

That’s actually part of what worries me, because I’ll be alone at home and I’ll think, “Okay, I can finally sit down and relax,” and then I just… can’t. I might be worn out, really tired, and still I feel like I need to get up and do the next thing. Not always because there’s some urgent thing that has to be done, but because I feel unsettled inside, like I can’t settle inside my own skin.

It’s like my body should be resting, but something in me is saying, “Get up, move, do something.” And I’ll sit for a minute and then I’m up again, or I’m thinking about what I should jump to next. So yes, it’s most of the time lately, not just in situations that make me nervous or where I’m being expected to sit still. That’s really why I came in, because it’s gotten to where I don’t feel like I can just be still anymore.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences akathisia-like symptoms that may point to a medication-related cause, which could help differentiate between the diagnostic possibilities.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt this inner restlessness or need to move after taking any medications, especially ones like antidepressants or antipsychotics?

target_item.name: Feeling_Restless
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I feel like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore, like I have to jump up and do the next thing even when I am worn out and should be sitting still.
target_item.reason: The question is most directly about the patient’s inner restlessness and need to move, which matches this symptom, even though it also asks about whether medications may trigger it.

patient.answer:
I honestly don’t know that I can say it happened after taking a certain medication. I don’t want to give you the wrong idea or act like I’ve clearly noticed, “Oh, I took this pill and then I couldn’t sit still,” because I haven’t really tracked it that way.

What I can say is that the reason I came in is this feeling that I just cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. It’s like I have to jump up and do the next thing, even when I’m worn out and should be sitting still. I’ll be tired, and I’ll know there’s no reason I need to get up right that second, but inside it feels like something is pushing me to move or do something.

So, as far as antidepressants or those kinds of medicines, I can’t honestly connect it to that. The restlessness is definitely there, though, and it’s gotten hard for me to ignore.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's restlessness is accompanied by significant distress or impairment in daily functioning, which would support a diagnosis of akathisia (F06.4) over others.
doctor.question: Has this inner restlessness made it hard for you to function in your usual daily activities, or caused you a lot of distress?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: My family has had to step in with bills and paperwork, and people at church and the garden have had to redo plans or cover responsibilities I dropped. I feel embarrassed because groups I care about no longer feel they can count on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms are causing distress or interfering with daily functioning, which directly matches the functional impairment item.

patient.answer:
Yes, it really has. I wish I could say it was just annoying, like just this private uncomfortable feeling, but it’s gone past that.

My family has had to step in with things I used to handle myself, like bills and paperwork, because I either don’t sit down long enough to finish them or I jump from one thing to another and leave it half done. And then it piles up, and then I feel ashamed, and then someone has to help me sort through it. That’s been hard, because I’ve always wanted to be seen as someone who can manage her own affairs.

And it’s affected other people too, not just at home. At church, and with the garden group, there have been times when I said I would take care of something or be responsible for part of a plan, and then I dropped it or didn’t follow through the way I should have. People had to redo plans or cover for me, and I could tell it frustrated them, even if they were kind about it.

That part really bothers me. I feel embarrassed, honestly. These are groups I care about, and I don’t want to be unreliable. But lately I feel like people don’t quite trust that they can count on me the way they used to, and that makes me feel awful. So yes, it’s caused a lot of distress, and it’s definitely interfering with my normal life.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences akathisia-like symptoms that may be related to medication use, which is important for differentiating between F90.0 (ADHD), F43.1 (PTSD), and F06.4 (psychotic disorder due to medical condition or medication).
doctor.question: Have you ever experienced this kind of restlessness or need to move when you started, stopped, or changed the dose of a medication, even if it was a long time ago?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether the restlessness is related to starting, stopping, or changing medication doses, which is not covered by any listed symptom profile item.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure, honestly. I’ve been trying to think back, because I know you’re asking whether there was some clear point where I started or stopped a medicine, or the dose changed, and then this restlessness showed up.

But I can’t really say that. I don’t have a memory of, “Oh, that happened right after a medication change.” I just don’t want to guess and accidentally make it sound like there’s a connection when I haven’t actually noticed one.

I mean, it may be that there were medication changes over the years and I just didn’t pay attention closely enough, but as I’m sitting here trying to remember, nothing stands out to me like that. What stands out is the restlessness itself and how hard it’s been to settle down, but I can’t tie it to starting, stopping, or changing a dose of something.

doctor.intent: Determine if the restlessness is accompanied by a compulsion to perform specific behaviors or mental acts in response to an obsession, which would support F43.1 (Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder) over other candidates.
doctor.question: Do you ever feel driven to do certain things over and over, like checking, counting, or fixing, because you can't get certain thoughts out of your head or because you feel something bad will happen if you don't?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about obsessive-compulsive symptoms such as repetitive checking, counting, or fixing driven by intrusive thoughts or fear something bad will happen, which is not covered by the provided ADHD symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so, not in the way you’re describing. I mean, I do sometimes go back and recheck things, but I think that’s more because I get distracted or I don’t trust that I finished something properly, not because I have a specific thought like, “If I don’t check this three times, something terrible will happen.”

I don’t really count things or have rituals like that, at least not that I’ve noticed. And I don’t feel like I’m fixing things over and over to stop some bad event from happening. It’s more that I’ll lose track, or I’ll feel unsettled and then I’m not sure what I already did. But I can’t say I have those stuck thoughts you’re talking about, where they force me to do a certain action in a certain way.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences akathisia-like symptoms that are not tied to medication use, which would support F06.4, or if symptoms are better explained by ADHD (F90.0) or adjustment with mixed anxiety and depressed mood (F43.1).
doctor.question: Have you always had trouble sitting still or feeling calm, even going back to when you were younger, or is this something that started more recently in your life?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Even back in grade school, my teachers wrote that I was bright but careless, always losing papers, talking out of turn, and needing reminders to stay in my seat or finish my work.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the restlessness and trouble sitting still were present when I was younger, which directly relates to symptom onset before age 12.

patient.answer:
Oh, it goes way back. It’s not something that just started recently, even though it feels worse or more noticeable now.

I actually remember seeing comments from teachers when I was in grade school — or my mother would mention them — that I was “bright but careless,” that kind of thing. They’d say I lost papers, talked when I wasn’t supposed to, didn’t stay with my work, or needed reminders to stay in my seat and finish what I was doing. At the time, I think people just thought I was careless or not trying hard enough, because I could understand the schoolwork, but I was always being corrected for the way I went about it.

So yes, the sitting still and settling myself, that has been there since I was young. It’s just that when you’re a child, people scold you or redirect you, and you don’t necessarily think of it as a pattern until much later.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a history of manic or hypomanic episodes to rule out bipolar disorder (F31.x).
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more where you felt extremely upbeat, unusually confident, or so energetic that you hardly needed sleep?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about possible manic or hypomanic episodes, such as elevated mood, unusual confidence, increased energy, and decreased need for sleep, which is not covered by the provided ADHD symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt keyed up or couldn’t settle, but not in the way you’re saying — like several days where I was unusually upbeat or full of confidence and barely sleeping and still feeling great.

I’m trying to be careful, because my energy can feel all over the place, and sometimes I’ll stay up too late or get wound up, but I don’t remember a stretch where I thought, “Wow, I don’t need sleep,” or where I was on top of the world for days. If anything, when I don’t sleep enough, I usually feel worse, not better.

So as far as I can tell, no, I haven’t had that kind of period.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a history of manic or hypomanic episodes, which would support a diagnosis of bipolar disorder (F31.0-F31.9) or related conditions, and rule out other differential diagnoses like ADHD (F90.0) or anxiety-related restlessness (F43.1).
doctor.question: Have you ever had a time when your mood was elevated, you felt unusually good or irritable for several days, and you were doing things more quickly, taking more chances, or talking more than usual?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about possible manic or hypomanic episodes, including elevated or irritable mood, increased speed/activity, risk-taking, or increased talking for several days. The provided ADHD symptom profile does not include a matching item for this mood-episode screening question.

patient.answer:
No, I don’t think I’ve had a time like that. I mean, I can get irritable, and I can talk more when I’m wound up or nervous or trying to explain myself, but I don’t remember it coming in a several-day stretch where my mood was unusually high or I felt like a different person.

And I don’t think I’ve had those times where I was suddenly doing everything faster, taking risks, or feeling unusually good in a way that other people would notice as odd. If I’m moving quickly or talking a lot, it’s usually more scattered than anything, not like I’m confident and energized for days. I’m trying to think back, but nothing like that really stands out to me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a history of akathisia, which could help differentiate between the remaining diagnostic candidates.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt a strong urge to move your legs or a discomfort in your legs that only gets better when you move them, especially at night or when resting?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about restless legs-type symptoms (leg discomfort or urge to move relieved by movement, especially at night/rest), which is not covered by the ADHD symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think I’ve noticed that as a clear pattern — like a strong urge in my legs that only gets better if I move them. I do shift around a lot when I’m sitting or trying to relax, but I can’t say it’s because of a specific uncomfortable feeling in my legs, especially at night.

So… I guess my answer would be no, not that I’m aware of. If it has happened, I haven’t recognized it that way.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a long-standing pattern of inattention and hyperactivity consistent with ADHD, which would support F90.0 (Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder) as the primary diagnosis.
doctor.question: Looking back at your adult life, have you often had trouble staying focused on tasks, felt constantly on the go, or struggled to organize your thoughts and activities, even when you weren’t under unusual stress?

target_item.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: I can sit down with the senior center newsletter or a choir schedule and start out fine, but after a few minutes I realize my eyes have gone over the same lines and I have no idea what I just read.
target_item.reason: The question asks about longstanding trouble staying focused on tasks, which directly matches sustained attention difficulty.

patient.answer:
Yes, the focus part especially. That’s been there a long time, not just when something stressful is going on.

Like, I can sit down with the senior center newsletter, or even something simple like a choir schedule, and I start out thinking, “Okay, I’m going to read this and make sure I know what’s happening.” And then a few minutes later I realize my eyes have been going over the same lines again and again, and I honestly couldn’t tell you what I just read. It’s not that the words are too hard or that I don’t care — it’s like my mind just slips away while I’m still looking at the page.

And then I’ll go back to the top and try again, and sometimes I do that two or three times. It makes me feel foolish, because these are not complicated things. They’re everyday things I should be able to keep track of. So yes, trouble staying focused has definitely been an issue for me as an adult.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a history of significant mood episodes (depression or mania) that could support a diagnosis of bipolar disorder or major depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period of time lasting two weeks or more where you felt so down, hopeless, or uninterested in life that it was hard to function, or a time when you felt unusually high, overly confident, or so energetic that others noticed something was off?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about major depressive episodes or manic/hypomanic periods, which are not covered by the ADHD symptom profile items provided.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I can say yes to either of those in a clear way. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt low or discouraged, like anyone does, especially when things pile up or I’m frustrated with myself, but I don’t know that I’ve had a solid two weeks where I was so hopeless or uninterested in life that I just couldn’t function. At least nothing that stands out to me that way.

And the unusually high part, no, I don’t think so. I’ve never had a stretch where I felt overly confident or so full of energy that other people were saying something was wrong. If anything, when I’m wound up, it’s more like I’m scattered or restless, not like I’m on top of the world.

So I guess my answer is… not that I’m aware of. I’d probably remember if it was that extreme, but I don’t think I’ve had that kind of episode.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a history of significant mood episodes (depression or mania) that could support a diagnosis of bipolar disorder (F31) or major depressive disorder (F32), which may help rule out other candidates like ADHD (F90.0) or anxiety (F43.1).
doctor.question: Have you ever had a time when your mood was so low or so high that someone close to you expressed concern about the change, even if it didn’t last very long?

target_item.reason: The doctor's question is about possible mood episodes, such as unusually low or high mood noticed by others. The provided symptom profile covers ADHD symptoms and related impairment/onset/duration, but does not include depressive, manic, or hypomanic mood episodes.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so, no. I mean, people close to me have probably noticed when I’m irritated or overwhelmed or quieter than usual, but I can’t remember anyone saying they were worried because my mood seemed extremely low or unusually high.

I’m trying to think back, because sometimes family will say things like, “Are you okay?” or “You seem off today,” but that’s more in the normal kind of way, not like they were alarmed by a big change in me. I don’t recall anyone pulling me aside or saying, “You’re not acting like yourself,” because I was too down or too energized or anything like that.

So… no, not that I can remember. If it happened, it wasn’t something that stood out to me as a major mood change.
